name: SRIT India
lm_rationale: Choice Capital Advisors — chittorgarh 2026 tracker: 1 mainboard IPO (100% positive, +8.51% avg listing gain) and 3 SME IPOs (67% positive, +13.40% avg); 4 issues, 3 positive listings. Clears the ≥50%/≥5% bar but not ≥15% avg gain.
net_proceeds: ₹12.86 Cr for capex on modernisation and redevelopment of existing products and ₹124.00 Cr for working capital (₹80.60 Cr in FY27, ₹43.40 Cr in FY28); the rest goes to unidentified acquisitions/strategic initiatives and general corporate purposes, capped together at 35% of gross proceeds.
key_risks: 89.41% of FY26 revenue came from Government tenders, the order book fell to ₹1,182.82 Cr in FY26 from ₹1,476.96 Cr in FY24, and operating cash flow was negative ₹12.10 Cr in FY26 as receivables and other current assets grew.
market_moat: 26-year track record with more than 103 projects worth ₹1,234.72 Cr executed over the last decade, and delivery processes appraised at CMMI Level 5 and SSE-CMM, which help it pre-qualify for large Government tenders.
management: Promoters Dr. Nambiar Raghavan Madhusoodan (MD & CEO), Prasaktha Vakkiyl Nambiar and Martin Poovakkulam Chacko; 84.91% pre-issue promoter holding drops to 62.71% post-issue.
prose_business: Bengaluru-based IT/ITeS company that builds, integrates and runs digital platforms, mainly for Government bodies, in three verticals: healthcare, e-governance, and telecom and broadband. Projects include hospital information systems, state-wide fibre networks, nationwide banking connectivity, AI traffic management and a forensic-lab integration project in Maharashtra. It also works abroad through its Qatar operations.
highlight_dev: The RHP describes its entry into the power utility sector with a transformer monitoring and digital monitoring project for a Karnataka Government power generation corporation's thermal stations.
sector_outlook: The RHP's D&B industry section, citing NASSCOM, says Indian IT-BPM revenue grew from USD 167.0 billion in FY2018 to USD 254.0 billion in FY2024.
gov_scheme: The RHP lists a GIS-based survey and middle-mile network development project for Rail Vikas Nigam Limited under the BharatNet DBOM model among the company's Government contracts.
peer_sentence: At 19.29x post-issue P/E, SRIT sits just above the RHP peer average of 18.31x (Mastek 12.59x, Allied Digital Services 15.52x, Aurionpro Solutions 18.62x, Protean eGov Technologies 19.80x, Railtel Corporation of India 24.03x).
verdict_reason: 30.23% RoNW and +28.82% PAT growth, but priced at peer average with negative FY26 operating cash flow
why: Revenue grew 15.58% to ₹450.00 Cr and PAT 28.82% to ₹43.29 Cr in FY26, with RoNW of 30.23% and D/E of 0.23. At ₹130 the issue is priced at 19.29x post-issue EPS and 3.19x NAV, in line with the RHP peer average of 18.31x, so there is little pricing discount. Most of the ₹218.40 Cr fresh issue funds working capital (₹124.00 Cr) and a small capex (₹12.86 Cr), but up to 35% can go to unidentified acquisitions and general corporate purposes. Choice Capital's 2026 bench is Solid (3 of 4 listings positive, modest gains). The main risk is dependence on Government tenders (89.41% of revenue) together with a shrinking order book and negative operating cash flow of ₹12.10 Cr in FY26.
suggestion: Apply only for long term; priced at the peer average, so listing gains depend on demand and GMP
discrepancies: Chittorgarh pre-IPO EPS 9.12 / P/E 14.25 (PAT ÷ current share count) vs RHP basic & diluted FY26 EPS ₹9.47, giving P/E 13.73 at ₹130; RHP used

Chittorgarh PAT margin 9.62% is PAT ÷ revenue from operations (RHP KPI); brief's formula PAT ÷ total income gives 9.36%; 9.36% used, RHP 9.62% noted
